messages.content:
Diagnosis:

The test that failed is checking how HelpFormatter breaks a long command-line argument description into multiple lines with wrapping, indentation, and width constraints. The test expects the output to be split and indented in a particular way (lines wrapped appropriately to fit width 22).

The current issue report states that if a single word in a description is longer than the allowed width, the HelpFormatter wrapping code enters an infinite loop until the JVM runs out of memory. This happens when there's not enough space to fit a whole word before wrapping is attempted.

Examining the HelpFormatter.printHelp method, we see it calls printUsage and then printWrapped for the header and footer, and importantly calls printOptions to print the options with wrapping and indentation.

The core part of wrapping text appears to be the renderWrappedText method. This method tries to find an appropriate wrap position (breaking point) within the specified width by calling findWrapPos. If no suitable break is found, it appends the text as is.

The wrapping loop in renderWrappedText repeatedly finds wrap points and appends lines until the entire text is processed. However, the bug appears here: inside the while(true) loop (lines 832-850), the logic modifies the text by trimming and padding but crucially relies on findWrapPos returning a valid wrap position. If findWrapPos returns a wrap position that doesn't advance forward in the string (especially when the word itself is longer than width and no spaces are found), then the substring taken won't consume any characters, so the new text remains the same or does not move forward, causing the loop to repeat infinitely.

The findWrapPos method attempts to find a whitespace character at or before the width limit to wrap on. If none is found, it looks for whitespace after the width. If no whitespace is found at all (typical for a very long single word), it returns -1. But in renderWrappedText, if text length is longer than width and the pos returned equals nextLineTabStop-1, it forcibly sets pos to width (line 846). This is supposed to prevent zero or no progress in the loop, but only triggers under a specific condition.

The infinite loop likely arises when findWrapPos returns a position that causes the substring calls in renderWrappedText not to reduce the size of the text string (i.e., the text.substring(pos) on line 834 does not advance or the adjusted pos condition is not hit).

Hence, when a word is longer than the width (or when indentations are configured such that the wrapping width becomes too small), the current logic does not properly break the word or move forward correctly, leading to repeated wrapping at the same position.

In the failing test, the issue may not have arisen if the long words get broken correctly, but with certain inputs and widths (as in the current bug report example), infinite loop and OutOfMemory occur due to failure to advance the substring position in the wrapping code.

Therefore, the root cause is:
- renderWrappedText's while loop does not correctly handle the case where no wrap can be found within width and text length > width with no break characters.
- findWrapPos returns a position or -1 that leads to no progress in substring trimming, leading to infinite loop in renderWrappedText.

This diagnosis matches the current bug report description and test symptoms of infinite loop in HelpFormatter wrapping.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this wrapping logic or infinite loop issue. They focus on option ordering or parsing, so they provide no useful additional insight.

# Short summary:
The infinite loop is caused by renderWrappedText's while loop failing to advance the substring position when wrapping a very long word that exceeds the given width, due to findWrapPos returning positions that do not make progress in substringing, which leads to repeated processing of the same text fragment indefinitely.

Potential fix: Change wrapping code to break a word forcibly if no whitespace is found within the width or improve the substring position logic to guarantee progress each iteration.

---

Next, I will identify which methods would be the best locations to fix this bug.
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(java.lang.StringBuffer,int,int,java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(java.lang.String,int,int)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
